subject: KV-cache backlog causing reserved throughput erosion — triage & exec ask
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@pinebridge.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: ops@pinebridge.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency + 5xx burst on reserved pool (stripe-42) — urgent

Markus / David —

We're hitting severe tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors against our reserved endpoints on stripe-42 starting ~08:45 PT. Median latency is OK but p95/p99 have ballooned (p99 ~3.8s) and customer's user-facing ingest is timing out at scale. The attaches show the error snippets and the top-of-stack trace pointing to repeated KV cache lookups (large prefix fanout).

This is hitting our month-to-month production flows and risking our SLA. We haven't changed client-side traffic shapes — this looks like a server-side resource contention/cold-cache scenario. Can you confirm whether this is a dedicated-reserved capacity degradation or a noisy neighbor spill? Pinebridge is on a committed reserved plan and will expect remediation.

Attaching: pinebridge_error_snaps.log

Samir
Senior Platform Engineer
Pinebridge Financial
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: david.kim@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@pinebridge.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx burst on reserved pool (stripe-42) — urgent

Thanks for the heads up, Samir — and thanks for the logs.

Quick read: this looks like a KV-cache backlog (hot prefixes) causing heavy read amplification at the runtime layer. The serving runtime is falling back to slower kernel paths under contention and we're seeing prefix eviction stalls — so reserved throughput is effectively eroded for this tenant. Not a happy state for a reserved customer.

Immediate asks (short-term):
- David: start targeted KV-cache eviction for Pinebridge compute shards; prioritize eviction for long-lived prefixes (I attached eviction-script.diff).
- Grace: open a burst authorization to ops for +2 GPUs on stripe-42 for the next 4 hours (we'll pay burst credits) — need exec sign-off if this becomes longer.
- Samir: if you can route a small fraction (5-10%) of traffic to the smaller-latency model (r-compact-1) we can offload the hot-path while we clear the cache.

I'll prepare a one-pager (initial-mitigation-plan.pdf) and flag the risk to leadership. Vivek — cc'ing you because this touches a committed reserved account and we should authorize ops burst if needed.

I'll update in 30 mins with current metrics.

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: david.kim@redwood.com <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@pinebridge.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 13:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx burst on reserved pool (stripe-42) — urgent

Ack. Rolling the targeted eviction now (INF-7821). Steps executed:
- Disabled long-lived prefix pinning for Pinebridge shards a,b,c
- Incremented eviction aggressiveness for those shards
- Pushed an optimized hot-path kernel fallback that reduces synchronous disk reads

Early signal: p95 improved from ~2.6s to ~1.1s within 8 minutes. 5xx rate down ~72%. Still seeing some queuing on the TTI plane; requesting immediate +2 GPU burst on stripe-42 while we observe for the next 90 minutes.

Attaching the eviction diff for audit: eviction-script.diff

I'll continue to monitor and share graphs.

—David
David Kim
Senior Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@pinebridge.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: KV-cache backlog causing reserved throughput erosion — triage & exec ask

Vivek — short summary and requested decision:

What happened: a concentrated set of hot prefixes in Pinebridge's workload caused KV-cache amplification and long-running eviction stalls in their dedicated shard set on stripe-42. That caused the runtime to choose slower execution kernels and queue tokens, which reduced the effective reserved throughput for that tenant and generated consumer-visible p99 spikes and a burst of 5xxs.

What we've done: targeted eviction + kernel fallback (David) + temporary routing recommendation (Markus). Early metrics show p99 and 5xx improving but we are not fully back to baseline; the cache thaw will take ~1-2 hours for steady state under current traffic.

Decision we need from execs: authorize a short burst (+2 GPUs) for stripe-42 for up to 4 hours while we stabilize. If approved we will:
- Give Pinebridge routing guidance to offload 5-10% to r-compact-1
- Keep eviction policy tightened for 3hrs then slowly relax
- Run a post-mortem and propose a KV-cache protection guardrail (throttle + proactive eviction) and a model-routing policy to avoid future reserved erosion.

Customer impact: medium (user timeouts) but improving; customer is watching SLA window closely.

Requested approval: APPROVE BURST (+2 GPUs, stripe-42, 4h) or DECLINE (we'll continue mitigation but will request longer credit + customer-facing note).

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
